why: Section 3 of CLAUDE_CODE_TASK.md prescribes shrinking VOXEL_MM when valve volume < 2.5 mL, on the premise that the remesh voxel is eating a 1 mm wall. The premise is false: the valve components are zero-thickness open sheets (every component has Euler characteristic 1 or 0 = disc/annulus, no enclosed volume), so the remesh film thickness is set by the voxel alone and shrinking the voxel makes it thinner.

measured_film_thickness_at_voxel_0.25_mm.note: = 1.11 x voxel; 2*V/A. Confirms thickness is a pure voxel artefact, not a preserved wall.

manifoldness: was never the failure mode - true at every voxel tested
fix_applied: SOLIDIFY 1.2 mm (centred, rim-capped) BEFORE the voxel remesh, in blender_pipeline.py. 1.2 mm is the value the script's own docstring already named as the intended solidify.
note_on_the_2.5_mL_floor: The 2.5-6.0 mL band was derived as area x 1 mm = 3.3 mL, which double-counts regions where leaflets overlap. A true 1.0 mm wall yields 2.21 mL (mitral) because the remesh unions the overlaps. At 1.2 mm both valves land in band and the measured wall is >= 1.0 mm over 99.8% of area.
